subjects.name: INTEGRATED PERSONALITY DEVELOPMENT COURSE-I
course_outcomes: 1. To provide students with a holistic value-based education that will enable them to be successful in their academic, professional, and social lives.
2. To give the students the tools to develop effective habits, promote personal growth, and improve their well being, stability, and productivity.
3. To allow students to establish a stronger connection with their family through critical thinking and development of qualities such as unity, forgiveness, empathy, and effective communication.
4. To provide students with soft skills that complement their hard skills, making them more marketable when entering the workforce.
5. To enhance awareness of India s glory and global values, and to create considerate citizens who strive for the betterment of their family, college, workforce, and nation.
6. To inspire students to strive for a higher sense of character by learning from role models who have lived principled, disciplined, and value-based lives.

Students will learn the importance of studying India¶s glorious past so that they could develop a strong passion and pride for our nation.

allSyllabusUnits.title: My India My Pride Glorious Past Part-2

allSyllabusUnits.title: Learning from Legends A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Dr Kalam¶s inspirational life displayed legendary qualities which apply to students (1) Dare to Dream (2) Work Hard (3) Get Good Guidance (4) Humility (5) Use Your Talents for the Benefit of Others

allSyllabusUnits.title: Soft Skills Networking & Leadership

allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn the secrets of project management through the Akshardham case study. They will then practice these skills through an activity relevant to student life.

allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn how social media can become addictive and they will imbibe simple methods to take back control.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Facing Failures Power of Faith
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn about the power and necessity of faith in our daily lives.

allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will understand the importance of strong family relationships. They will learn how to overcome the generation gap and connect with their family more.

Questions: [8 marks] A student must apply engineering curves and their practical classification in a practical situation such as selecting a curve construction for a cam profile or motion diagram. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply constructing an ellipse by standard geometric methods in a practical situation such as drawing an ellipse when the major and minor axes are known. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply parabola and hyperbola construction and the focus/directrix idea in a practical situation such as constructing a conic using a given focus and directrix. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply cycloidal curves, involutes and spirals in a practical situation such as representing a point on a rolling circle or an unwinding string. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.
Answers:
Model answer:
Engineering curves include conics and other geometric curves used to represent shapes or motion. Ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas are conic sections; cycloids, epicycloids, hypocycloids, involutes and spirals are other common constructions in engineering graphics. The method is chosen according to the defining geometry and the intended use. A drawing should show construction lines clearly, use suitable instruments and identify the required tangent or normal when requested. Accuracy depends on the construction procedure and neat, unambiguous line work.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should connect the concept to the stated example, explain the steps in order and justify the outcome.

Model answer:
An ellipse can be constructed by methods such as concentric circles, rectangle or oblong methods, and arc-of-circle approaches taught in the syllabus. First mark the major and minor axes and their centres accurately. Divide the relevant circles, sides or arcs into corresponding parts, project matching points and draw a smooth continuous curve through them. Select the method according to the data and construction requested. Check symmetry about both axes and use light construction lines before darkening the final curve.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should connect the concept to the stated example, explain the steps in order and justify the outcome.

Model answer:
A conic is defined by a geometric relation between a point and a focus/directrix or by another specified construction condition. A parabola has eccentricity one; an ellipse has eccentricity below one and a hyperbola above one. Construction methods use the given dimensions or geometric properties to locate successive points, then join them smoothly. Tangents and normals are drawn according to the prescribed method at the required point. Verify the defining dimensions and symmetry and distinguish the conics by their geometry rather than by appearance alone.

A strong answer should connect the concept to the stated example, explain the steps in order and justify the outcome.

Model answer:
A cycloid is traced by a point on a circle rolling along a straight line. An epicycloid is generated when a circle rolls outside another circle, while a hypocycloid is generated when it rolls inside. An involute can be understood as the path traced by the end of a taut string unwound from a base curve; spirals move progressively inward or outward according to their construction. Start from the generating geometry, divide the motion into corresponding steps, plot points carefully and construct any requested tangent or normal.

Questions: [8 marks] A student must apply drawing instruments, bis conventions, line types and layout in a practical situation such as preparing a standards-based engineering sheet before drawing a component. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply representative fraction and selection of drawing scales in a practical situation such as choosing a scale to fit a large object on a small sheet. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply dimensioning and annotation of engineering drawings in a practical situation such as making a component drawing usable by a workshop without verbal explanation. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.

[8 marks] A student must apply orthographic projection and first-angle versus third-angle methods in a practical situation such as producing front, top and side views from a pictorial object. Explain the method or reasoning, set out the main steps, and justify the result.
Answers:
Model answer:
A drawing sheet should have a suitable size, border, title block and layout, with space allocated for views and notes. Instruments such as drawing boards, T-squares or parallel rules, set squares, compass, divider and scale support accurate construction. Standard line conventions distinguish visible outlines, hidden edges, centre lines, dimensions and construction work. Use lettering and dimensioning consistently and choose a suitable scale when the object will not fit at full size. Standards make drawings legible and interpretable by others, rather than relying on informal assumptions.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should connect the concept to the stated example, explain the steps in order and justify the outcome.

Model answer:
Representative fraction (RF) is drawing length divided by actual length after both are expressed in the same units. A full-size scale has RF 1:1; a reducing scale has RF below one, and an enlarging scale has RF greater than one. For example, RF 1:5 means a 50 mm actual length is shown as 10 mm on the drawing. Select a scale that preserves legibility and available sheet space, state it clearly, and apply it consistently to dimensions and construction. The written dimension normally states actual size, not the measured paper length.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should connect the concept to the stated example, explain the steps in order and justify the outcome.

Model answer:
Dimensioning communicates the size and position of features. Use clear extension and dimension lines, legible figures and appropriate symbols, and avoid repeating dimensions or creating ambiguity. Choose line types according to their purpose: visible outlines, hidden details, centre lines and dimension lines should be distinguishable. Annotations should be placed near the relevant feature without clutter. A drawing should contain enough dimensions to manufacture or inspect the part, but not contradictory or redundant values. Apply the relevant standard conventions and check units and overall dimensions.

A strong answer should connect the concept to the stated example, explain the steps in order and justify the outcome.

Model answer:
Orthographic projection represents an object through views perpendicular to principal planes. The front view communicates height and width, the top view width and depth, and a side view height and depth. In first-angle projection, the object is between the observer and projection plane; in third-angle projection, the projection plane is between observer and object. Therefore the arrangement of views differs. Identify the projection method by its symbol or stated convention, align corresponding dimensions across views, and check that the set of views describes one consistent object.
